Reuters witnesses heard blasts in Moscow and saw plumes of smoke billowing from the refinery site. It was not clear what damage the facility had sustained. title: S. Korea wins women's team bronze in soft tennis
snippet: NAGOYA, Japan — South Korea won bronze in the women's team event in soft tennis at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on Sunday, its first medal in the sport at this year's competition. South Korea lost to Chinese Taipei 2-1 in the semifinals at Nagoya City Higashiyama Park Tennis Center in Nagoya, central Japan. There is no bronze medal contest in soft tennis and the two losers of the semifinals are both awarded bronze medals. snippet: Saudi Arabia withdraws from China-led digital currency platform Saudi Arabia has pulled out of a China-led digital currency platform aimed at facilitating cross-border payments outside the US dollar, the Financial Times (FT) reported. Riyadh joined the mBridge project in 2024 with China, Hong Kong, Thailand, the United Arab Emirates and the Bank for International Settlements, but the Saudi Central Bank said that it completed its participation in May 2025. The mBridge platform uses blockchain technology that allows central banks to make transactions directly via digital currencies, which could reduce transaction costs and the dollar’s intermediary role. The Saudi Central Bank said it was involved as part of a planned research programme and it was no longer a participating member after completing its proof of concept. But the FT reported that a second person familiar with the matter said the Saudi central bank remained quietly involved with the project.
